text:
sam_cs: FYI — multiple customers (Acme, Helix, and one smaller account) hitting 503s on multipart embedding streams since ~09:12 UTC. Gateway shows upstream worker exits and immediate 503s. Quick log snippet from one affected runner:
```
[09:11:56] runtime: allocating GPU memory failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
[09:11:56] infer-runner[pid=2345]: Assertion `kv_cache != NULL' failed. Segmentation fault (core dumped)
[09:11:57] orchestrator: container restart (exit 139)
```
sam_cs: Opening ticket INC-2026-045 and looping in CS. Customers report timeouts and retries, some billing noise from repeated requests.

melissa_oncall: Acknowledged. Oncall here — any deploys in the last 2 hours? If not, we should apply a routing mitigation and communicate. Can we route affected tenants to a fallback model variant?

arjun_eng: No prod deploys in the past 2h. Reproducer: multiplexed streaming embed requests with many small parts + parallel clients triggers high ephemeral KV/cache allocation and OOM. Quick repro curl (sanitized):
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings/stream \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -F "file=@parts.ndjson" \n  -F "model=huge-embed-v2"\n  -F "stream=true"
```
Running that with ~40 concurrent connections on a single runner pushes per-GPU RSS to >95% and the process dies (exit 139).

infra-bot: automated: fallback routing applied for tenants: Acme, Helix. Policy: route to small-embed-v1 for new requests. Telemetry: detected GPU mem spike at 09:11:50 -> 09:12:05, +62% requests failed with 503.

melissa_oncall: Good. Sam, please ask CS to throttle concurrency for affected customers and provide a short customer-facing note. Also please stash a list of affected API keys for billing credits assessment.

sam_cs: Will do. CS draft ready in #customer-success for review. Note: some customers reported doubled token charges due to retries; request finance review for potential credits.

arjun_eng: Short-term mitigations we pushed to the autoscaler/config: 1) pin model to small-embed-v1 for affected tenants, 2) set REDWOOD_POOL_MAX_BATCH=8 on the pool, 3) disable KV prefetch for multipart streams (config toggle). These reduce memory pressure immediately. Medium-term: patch to allocator to better handle fragmented KV allocations.

nvdiag: Action items for debugging: capture 60s nvidia-smi dmon, `docker logs --since 09:10`, and a GDB backtrace for crashed pid. Commands I ran earlier (adapt and run on impacted host):
```bash
# nvml trace
nvidia-smi dmon -s u -d 1 -o TD & sleep 60; pkill -f "nvidia-smi dmon"
# kernel logs
sudo journalctl -k --since "2026-03-18 09:05:00" > /tmp/kern.log
# gdb bt (replace <pid>)
sudo gdb --batch -ex "thread apply all bt full" -p <pid> > /tmp/gdb_bt.txt
```
Please upload outputs to /mnt/incident/INC-2026-045. Also capture `ulimit -a` for the runner container and the exact command line used to launch the inference process.

melissa_oncall: I've scheduled a sync with Acme at 10:15 UTC to explain mitigations. Draft posted in #customer-success for review.

sam_cs: Tracking: ticket INC-2026-045, internal incident tracker ID INC-2026-045. Next: arjun to attach heap snapshot and gdb trace by EOD, nvdiag to gather nvml/profile logs, melissa to finalize CS comms and billing review. Leaving fallback routing enabled until we confirm patch. :thumbsup:

arjun_eng: Will upload a minimal heap snapshot and stack trace to the incident folder in ~3 hours. Working hypothesis: fragmented KV allocations + multiplexed streaming exposing an allocator race under high parallelism.

infra-bot: note: autoscaler made 3 attempts to respin containers during the spike; we observed a respawn loop on 10.12.4.7 between 09:12:00 and 09:13:30.

sam_cs: If anyone finds a quick hotfix we can apply at the pool level, ping here. Otherwise we'll keep routing and throttles in place and update customers.
